newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia 10-year govt bond average yield 6.812 pct.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia 10-year govt bond average yield 6.812 pct.

text.p: Bank Negara Malaysia said it accepted bids at an average yield of 6.812 percent for a 10-year Malaysian government bond issue for two billion ringgit.
It said the bids accepted were in a high/low range of 6.82/77 percent.
Bank Negara said at 6.81 percent yield, the price of the bond worked out to 100.014 ringgit. At 6.78 percent the price was 100.227 ringgit.
Money market dealers said the bond was trading at a yield of 6.79 to 6.81 percent ahead of the tender's results.
The Malaysian Government Securities, as the bonds are called, are issued by Bank Negara on behalf of the Government.
The number of MGS issues has fallen over the last few years as the government has privatised most state-owned companies and infrastructure projects.
This is the third MGS issue this year. In June, the government raised two billion ringgit from the issue of five-year bonds at a coupon of 6.48 percent.
In September, it issued seven-year government bonds to raise two billion ringgit at a coupon of 6.586 percent.

Dealers said the latest bond issue would mop up liquidity arising from some large Bank Negara bill and deposit maturities and roll over two maturing MGS issues totalling 1.1 billion ringgit on December 15.
